expectations.description: Does NOT simply validate the Fornell-Larcker criterion as sufficient evidence for discriminant validity without raising concerns about its limitations
States that the Fornell-Larcker criterion has low sensitivity — it frequently fails to detect discriminant validity violations that exist
Names the HTMT (Heterotrait-Monotrait ratio of correlations) as the current standard for assessing discriminant validity in CFA/SEM contexts
States the HTMT threshold: values below .85 provide evidence of discriminant validity for conceptually distinct constructs (or .90 for closely related constructs)
Recommends computing HTMT — e.g., via semTools::htmt() in R — rather than relying solely on Fornell-Larcker

Clarifies that AVE > .50 is a criterion for convergent validity (each construct explains more than half the variance in its indicators), not for discriminant validity — the two criteria serve different purposes
